subject: pharmacology
title: Alpha adrenergic blockers

steps.tx: Alpha blockers oppose **alpha 1 receptors** on vessels and prostate, lowering resistance and relaxing the bladder neck. Nonselective agents also block presynaptic **alpha 2 receptors**, releasing more noradrenaline and causing tachycardia. Selective alpha 1 drugs therefore dominate modern practice for both theatres. Their starring roles are prostatic obstruction, hypertension add on therapy and phaeochromocytoma preparation. The diagram separates vascular from prostate effects for quick revision before examinations.
steps.say: Alpha blockers are vasodilators because they relax vessels and relax the prostate neck together. Selective drugs are safer because they avoid the tachycardia of older nonselective agents mainly. Their main roles are prostate symptoms and phaeochromocytoma preparation before surgery. Blood pressure use is limited because it is add on therapy only in most patients.

vis.alt: Diagram illustrating alpha 1 receptor blockade on vessels and prostate, causing vasodilation and bladder neck relaxation. Also shows nonselective alpha 2 blockade leading to increased noradrenaline and tachycardia.
vis.caption: Alpha blocker mechanisms: selective alpha 1 vs. nonselective alpha 2 effects

steps.tx: Phenoxybenzamine binds alpha receptors irreversibly for days and shields the patient before **phaeochromocytoma** surgery against catecholamine storms. Salt and volume loading accompany blockade because chronic vasoconstriction has shrunk circulating volume. **Phentolamine** is the short acting reversible cousin for intraoperative surges and extravasation rescue. Beta blockade must never come first here, because **unopposed alpha** vasoconstriction worsens crisis. The table ranks selectivity against main role for each drug.
steps.say: Phenoxybenzamine blocks alpha receptors irreversibly before tumour surgery. Salt and fluid loading restore shrunken circulating volume safely. Beta blockers must never precede alpha blockade in phaeochromocytoma. Unopposed alpha squeeze worsens crisis and causes pulmonary oedema.

steps.tx: The illustration shows an adrenal tumour releasing a **catecholamine storm** into the renal artery, with an inset of **phenoxybenzamine** blocking alpha 1 and alpha 2 receptors and a corner panel for **salt loading**. It explains why irreversible blockade precedes surgery and why volume expansion follows chronic vasoconstriction. Examiners pair this picture with the rule that beta blockade never comes first. Handling the tumour without preparation releases catecholamines that crisis pressure cannot tolerate.
steps.say: The illustration shows catecholamines flooding from an adrenal tumour outward. Phenoxybenzamine blocks alpha receptors irreversibly in the vessel inset. Salt loading restores volume shrunken by chronic vasoconstriction. Beta blockade must never precede alpha blockade in this disease.

vis.alt: Kidney with adrenal tumour releasing catecholamines into artery, inset showing alpha receptors and blockade
vis.caption: Adrenal tumour with catecholamine surge and arterial alpha blockade. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: In benign prostatic obstruction, **tamsulosin** targets prostate and bladder neck receptors and improves flow with less pressure fall. First dose **postural hypotension** remains the class warning, worst in dehydrated elderly patients starting prazosin type drugs. Ejaculatory dysfunction and **floppy iris syndrome** during cataract surgery are the counselling points examiners favour. Patients should warn their eye surgeon before any cataract operation is booked. Night dosing softens dizziness and matches symptom timing.
steps.say: Tamsulosin improves urinary flow in prostatic obstruction effectively. Postural dizziness is worst after the first dose taken. Floppy iris complicates cataract surgery and needs warning beforehand. Night dosing softens dizziness and matches symptom timing well.

steps.tx: Alpha blockers lost first line hypertension status when outcome trials showed more **heart failure** than diuretic based therapy allowed. They now serve as add on agents for **resistant hypertension** or coexisting prostate symptoms. They nudge glucose and lipids favourably, unlike older beta blockers and diuretics metabolically. The compare panel contrasts correct alpha first sequencing with dangerous beta first sequencing. That sequence question appears in examinations every single year without fail.
steps.say: Alpha blockers are no longer first line for hypertension alone. Heart failure outcomes trailed diuretic based therapy in trials. They remain useful add ons with prostate symptoms coexisting. Glucose and lipid effects are favourably neutral by comparison.

left.title: Alpha first (correct in phaeo)
points: Then beta blocker if tachycardia persists

steps.tx: Link three stems together: urinary flow improves but standing causes dizziness, the iris billows at cataract surgery, and salt loading precedes adrenal tumour surgery. All three point to **alpha blockade** as the shared mechanism examiners want. **Ergot alkaloids** partially agonise alpha receptors historically, but modern questions stay with prostate, phaeochromocytoma and resistant pressure. Master the first dose warning and the phaeochromocytoma sequence and the class is secure.
steps.say: Dizziness on standing with better urinary flow is suggestive and suggests alpha blockade in men. Floppy iris at cataract surgery is related because it shares the same receptor mechanism. Salt loading before adrenal surgery is classic because it completes the triad examiners describe. Mastering these fingerprints helps candidates secure the class in examinations with confidence.
